metadata.description: Recursive self-replicating npm supply chain worm. Patient Zero: rxnt-authentication v0.0.3. Payload sweeps credentials, downloads TruffleHog, abuses GitHub APIs, and — critically — publishes poisoned versions of all victim packages, making each victim a new distribution node. 500+ versions across 796 packages compromised. Models a single propagation depth.

path.description: Initial compromise of Patient Zero (rxnt-authentication maintainer). Assessed as reuse of credentials leaked during the S1ngularity campaign — credential use is always #4. Alternative hypothesis: phishing (#9). The causal ambiguity shows how DRE: C from one campaign becomes the entry vector for the next.
path.evidence: Assessed with moderate confidence as credential reuse from S1ngularity campaign. Datadog Security Research.

path.description: Trojanized rxnt-authentication v0.0.3 published via legitimate npm publish API (September 14, 17:58 UTC). Package integrity compromised.

dre.title: Patient Zero Package Compromised
dre.desc: rxnt-authentication v0.0.3 published with bundle.js (3MB+) worm payload.

path.evidence: npm registry timestamp; Sonatype analysis of bundle.js payload.

path.description: Trust Acceptance Event (Update Vector / #10.1). Victim1 installs the compromised package version through normal dependency resolution. npm serves as transit infrastructure.
Package manager resolves, downloads, unpacks, and processes the package — preparing the lifecycle hook environment.
Postinstall hook triggers bundle.js (3MB+). R-EXEC: first FEC execution on Victim1's machine. Shai-Hulud 2.0 escalated to preinstall execution for earlier interception.
path.evidence: bundle.js payload analysis; Trend Micro report.

path.description: Filesystem credential sweep: .npmrc (npm tokens), .gitconfig (GitHub PATs), AWS credential files (~/.aws/credentials), GCP JSON service account keys. Standard filesystem read operations — data stays data.

dre.title: Credential Sweep
dre.desc: npm tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS credentials, and GCP keys harvested from victim's filesystem.

path.evidence: Credential file paths enumerated in bundle.js; Datadog analysis.

path.description: TruffleHog downloaded and executed for deeper secret scanning. R-EXEC: separate #7 step. The malware's act of downloading and running TruffleHog is the foreign-code event, regardless of TruffleHog being a legitimate tool.
path.evidence: TruffleHog binary download observed in network analysis.

path.description: TruffleHog scans the filesystem for secrets using its designed pattern-matching capabilities. Legitimate tool, legitimate function, abused scope.

dre.title: Deep Secret Scan
dre.desc: TruffleHog's pattern-matching reveals additional secrets beyond standard credential file locations.

path.description: Stolen GitHub tokens used to authenticate as Victim1. R-CRED: credential use is always #4.

Legitimate GitHub APIs abused to: create public 'Shai-Hulud' repository with exfiltrated secrets, inject malicious GitHub Actions workflows into every accessible repository, create pull requests, and convert private repositories to public.

dre.title: GitHub Abuse — Secrets Exposed & Repos Modified
dre.desc: Exfiltrated secrets committed to public repo (LoC). Malicious workflows injected, private repos made public (LoI).

bizRisk.title: Organizational Code & Secret Exposure
bizRisk.desc: Private repositories converted to public; secrets committed to attacker-controlled repos; malicious workflows injected across victim's GitHub presence.

path.evidence: Shai-Hulud named repos observed across multiple GitHub accounts; ArmorCode report.

path.description: Stolen npm tokens used to authenticate as Victim1 on the npm registry. R-CRED: credential use is always #4. This step initiates the worm's propagation phase.

For each package Victim1 maintains: retrieve package list sorted by download count (maximize blast radius), inject bundle.js into postinstall script, publish new version. Legitimate npm API, abused scope. Creates the recursive propagation vector.

dre.title: Worm Self-Replication
dre.desc: All of Victim1's npm packages poisoned with worm payload. Each becomes a new infection vector.

bizRisk.title: Exponential Supply Chain Propagation
bizRisk.desc: Each compromised maintainer's packages become new worm vectors. 500+ versions across 796 packages within days.

path.description: Recursive Trust Acceptance Event (Update Vector / #10.1). Each newly poisoned package creates a new TAE for downstream consumers. The attack path loops back to step 4 for each new victim — cyclic/fractal propagation. The conventional linear model of supply chain risk fails here.
path.evidence: Propagation pattern documented by Datadog, Sonatype, and Trend Micro.

path.description: Shai-Hulud 2.0 conditional destructive fallback: if exfiltration fails entirely, recursively overwrite and delete the victim's home directory. OS delete operations are legitimate; their scope is abused. DRE: Ac — files permanently inaccessible (not Availability loss). Different DRE, different recovery playbook: Ac calls for backups, not failover.

dre.title: Destructive Fallback — Home Directory Wipe
dre.desc: Conditional: if primary exfiltration fails, victim's home directory recursively deleted. Loss of Accessibility (not Availability).

bizRisk.title: Data Destruction
bizRisk.desc: Complete loss of user data, local credentials, configuration, and project files. Recovery requires backups.

path.evidence: Shai-Hulud 2.0 (November 2025) variant analysis; Trend Micro report.
